clue.text: Tetchy guests for fishmongers, for instance

definitions.note: plural in the clue because the Fishmongers is the name of one guild

parts.note: livery is an old adjective meaning liverish, irritable or tetchy
guests at your home are company

explanation.surface: Grumpy visitors arrive for the people who sell fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fishmongers' Company is one of the old trade guilds of the City of London, which are known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fishmongers is one example of a City of London guild of this kind.

clue.text: Like Cambridge, as opposed to Oxford, blue in boat

definitions.text: Like Cambridge, as opposed to Oxford, blue
definitions.meaning: Cambridge blue is a pale shade, Oxford blue a dark one, so the first is paler
a flat-bottomed barge used to carry goods to and from ships

explanation.surface: A rowing comment about the Varsity crews and the shades of blue they wear in the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford and Cambridge universities' colours are dark blue and light blue respectively; the boat suggests the Boat Race, but it is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge blue is paler than Oxford blue, and a flat barge for unloading ships has the same name.

clue.text: One who takes his bow before starting to play

definitions.text: One who takes his bow before starting to play

parts.words: One who takes his bow before starting to play
parts.note: a performer usually bows at the end, but this musician picks up a bow to draw across strings before playing

explanation.surface: A performer bows to the audience before the show begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A string player picks up the bow, the stick strung with horsehair, before making any music.

clue.text: Attempt to answer fresh questions about what MPs do

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
Members of Parliament sit in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: An exam on the business of parliamentarians.
explanation.definitionFit: A second sitting of an examination, taken after failing the first.

clue.text: Fish on the Spey, say, having fellow-director along for the ride?

parts.note: the cod is a common sea fish
the Spey is a Scottish salmon river

explanation.surface: An angler fishing on a Scottish salmon river with a colleague from the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: someone who shares the driving, here pictured as a fellow director along for the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A second driver in a rally car steers alongside the main one, like a joint director.

clue.text: Strong points of letters in Times editor finally included

indicators.note: included means one piece is put inside the other
the letters in the word Times are to be taken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word editor

explanation.surface: Praise for a newspaper's letters page and its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters in' turns TIMES into MEITS; 'finally' gives R from editor, and 'included' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Merits are the good qualities or strengths of something.

clue.text: Assent as concise as it could be

indicators.note: as it could be suggests the letters arranged another possible way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Agreeing as briefly as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it could be' rearranges AS and CONCISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Accession is agreement or consent to a proposal or treaty.

clue.text: Flower you usually can cultivate after collecting all the heads

indicators.note: heads are first letters, collected from the words before and after

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: you can generally grow this bloom once you have gathered the flower heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a link word but its first letter is the last one needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a plant with spiky leaves and tall spikes of white bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Tack round opponents bidding to finish

indicators.note: round says the first piece goes about the second

parts.note: a sailing boat tacks or veers when it changes course
in bridge North and East are opposing players in the bidding

explanation.surface: A sailing or bridge instruction about changing course to end the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play against East-West, so N and E are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer giving furniture its outer finish.

clue.text: Provided with translation done in Japan, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a text with glosses has explanations or translations of its words
japan is a hard black lacquer, so japanned work is shiny

explanation.surface: A text with a translation made in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: Japan with a small j is a lacquer, and a japanned surface is shiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Annotated with explanatory notes, and given a shiny finish like lacquer.

clue.text: Last in 'Tudor English song series put to new use

indicators.note: the last letter in the word Tudor is taken

parts.note: a song cycle is a set of songs performed as a series

explanation.surface: The final item in a series of Tudor English songs, reused.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle is to process waste so it can be used again.

clue.text: Stain article in colour

indicators.note: in says the article sits inside the word for colour

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Advice about removing a coloured mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or a moral blemish.

clue.text: Not willing to write in the empty ceremonious style

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: empty says only the outside letters of the word the are kept

parts.note: lying in state is lying with full ceremony

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to write in the stuffy ceremonial manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' is a pun on making a will: the person never wrote one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies without having made a will has left no testament.

clue.text: They can cope with sledging when they go for runs

definitions.text: They can cope with sledging when they go for runs

parts.words: They can cope with sledging when they go for runs
parts.note: reads like cricketers enduring verbal abuse from fielders while batting, but means animals hauling sledges over snow

explanation.surface: Batsmen who keep their nerve under taunts while running between the wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: Sledging in cricket is taunting the batsman; here it is literally pulling sledges.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic deer that pull sleds over snow on long journeys.

clue.text: Pharmacist is parking in more crowded location

indicators.note: in says those pieces go inside the location

parts.note: a denser place is more crowded
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: A chemist leaves the car in a busier spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist who makes up prescriptions dispenses drugs.

clue.text: Monogram for a nonentity

definitions.meaning: a person of no importance, a mere zero

explanation.surface: A set of initials for someone unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an interwoven design of initials and a nobody, a mere zero.

clue.text: Irresponsible sort of driver in collision with hare

parts.note: a hit is a collision or strike
and means together with
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist strikes a hare on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hare' is a verb, to run fast, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who strikes someone and flees the scene without stopping.

clue.text: Fish making the king ill it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the words are heard spoken

parts.note: GR, George Rex, is the king, and ailing means ill

explanation.surface: Food poisoning from a fish dish made the monarch sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater game fish with a large dorsal fin.

clue.text: Risk une's life, ultimately, in piece of folly

parts.note: to bet is to risk money on a result
one is I, and 's stands for is

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of the word life

explanation.surface: Gambling one's life away is a foolish act.
explanation.walkthrough: A bêtise is a French-derived word for a silly act; 'one's' is read as I + 'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish or stupid act or remark, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Feline creature taking short cut around tradesman's entrance

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
ca, circa, means around

indicators.note: entrance points to the opening letter of the word tradesman's

explanation.surface: A cat slips through the shortcut by the tradesman's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: A tradesman's entrance is a side or back door for deliveries in a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American wild cat with a short tail.

clue.text: Beast about to catch girl — that's not fair

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a brute is a beast
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A monster tries to grab a girl, and she protests at the injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fair' looks like an outburst but means not fair-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark brown hair, not a blonde.

clue.text: Penguin's partner?

parts.note: reads as a mate for the bird, but means the wife of an emperor, as in the emperor penguin

explanation.surface: Who is the bird's mate?
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor's wife is his consort; the emperor penguin gives the link.

clue.text: Endless battle between old sailors for sausage

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is taken away

parts.note: Salamis was the sea battle between Greeks and Persians in 480 BC

explanation.surface: Seafarers fight over a spicy meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a highly seasoned Italian dried sausage.

clue.text: Change of Rugby date to do with financial plan

indicators.note: change of says the letters of the following words are altered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Moving the date of a rugby match affects the finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the annual statement of planned public spending and revenue.

clue.text: Tough material split in two in sudden impact

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the clue words, split across the two of them

explanation.surface: Fabric torn apart by a sudden blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill used for jeans.

clue.text: Ladder raised to build quickly

parts.note: a ladder in tights is a run
raised means up

explanation.surface: Hoisting a ladder to put up a building fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in British usage is a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up a garment or shed is to make it hastily.

clue.text: Celebration both sides hold the night before

indicators.note: hold says the sides contain the next piece

parts.note: R and L are right and left, both sides
eve is the evening before a festival

explanation.surface: A party on both sides of the night before a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively party or festivity.

clue.text: Is a name recollected? Then this isn't complete

definitions.text: Is a name recollected? Then this isn't complete

indicators.note: recollected read as collected again, so the letters are regathered in a new order

explanation.surface: If you remember a name, your memory loss is only partial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges IS A NAME; the whole clue says remembering a name means the loss of memory is partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is partial if a person's name can still be recalled.

clue.text: A direct opposite is never totally different

indicators.note: totally different says the letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A truly opposite thing is never entirely unlike.
explanation.definitionFit: An inverse is the exact reverse or contrary of something.

clue.text: Official recognition of union

parts.note: sounds like a trade union being recognised, but means the certificate of a wedding

explanation.surface: Bosses formally acknowledge a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: A British term for a marriage certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: The document certifying that a couple have wed.
